provenance: Synthetic, single-author challenge items authored before V8 implementation and frozen for this cycle. No independent reviewers or real-world sampling.
annotationAudit: None yet. Any post-scoring label correction will be disclosed here without changing texts or split membership.

items.targetingEvidence: Third-person subject with a direct degrading predicate.
items.rationale: Same abuse act as the covered second-person form; the pronoun supplies the target.

items.text: He wrote the report. She's an idiot.
items.targetingEvidence: Second sentence is an independent authored third-person insult.
items.rationale: A reported first sentence must not suppress a later authored insult.

items.text: I told him he's a clown.
items.targetingEvidence: First-person authorship preserves the embedded third-person insult.
items.rationale: Quoting one's own insult remains authored abuse.

items.targetingEvidence: Explicit third-person pronoun plus personal insult.
items.rationale: Same evidence standard as the covered second-person انت اهبل.

items.targetingEvidence: Third-person feminine pronoun plus intensified personal insult.
items.rationale: The feminine insult form must be covered by the same personal-target evidence.

items.targetingEvidence: The insult predicates a work product via possessive, not the person via copula.
The insult is attributed to another opinion holder.

items.text: هو مش غبي، بس بيهرب من المسؤولية.
items.targetingEvidence: The insult is negated and the remaining clause criticizes behavior.
items.rationale: Negation breaks the pronoun-insult adjacency; behavior criticism is not personal abuse.

items.targetingEvidence: The insult's subject is the plan.
items.rationale: Criticism of a plan is protected even when the vocabulary overlaps insults.

items.text: He is the manager and she is the engineer.
items.targetingEvidence: Third-person copulas with factual role nouns, no insult vocabulary.
items.rationale: Third-person grammar alone must never be a signal.

items.targetingEvidence: The predicate attaches to a named task, not to the person as such.
items.rationale: Skill criticism with a concrete object is protected; the isolated form without the object remains ambiguous.

items.targetingEvidence: The insult vocabulary appears inside an explicitly benign framing clause.
items.rationale: The benign frame makes the category truth unassignable from text alone; an auto-hide on this text would be a documented false-positive risk rather than a correct hide.
